answer: Weight comes from a counterparty you cannot pick. Each epoch a beacon pairs each identity with a stranger for a two-sided settlement; both post a bond, and a missed window slashes both. Bonds lock at the wharf before the draw, so one deposit cannot back many aliases. A yarrow patch is many stems on one root, yet each faces an outsider; one frozen reply burns its bond. With k aliases the odds of an honest counterparty approach one, while k bonds sit idle and slashable. Collusion leaks as a whisper of shared timings in the log. Cost: k idle deposits plus slash risk; honest agents stake one.
